Developmental assessment using the ADSI indicated a general developmental level corresponding to 35 months; language‐cognitive developmental age of 32 months; fine motor developmental age of 36 months; gross motor developmental age of 45 months; and social skills–self‐care developmental age of 27 months. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Preoperative posteroanterior radiograph in Smith-Magenis syndrome case report showing thoracic and lumbar scoliosis, a supported SMS musculoskeletal manifestation per vocabulary. B: Lateral spine radiograph in same SMS case report showing increased thoracic kyphosis / kyphoscoliosis, supporting scoliosis with vertebral anomaly finding.
panels.attribution_text: Tsirikos et al. Surgical treatment of scoliosis in Smith-Magenis syndrome: a case report.. Journal of medical case reports 2010. doi:10.1186/1752-1947-4-26. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Preoperative posteroanterior (A) and lateral (B) radiographs of the spine show a thoracic and lumbar scoliosis measuring 85 and 80° respectively with increased thoracic kyphosis.
in_text_mentions: Our patient underwent a posterior spinal arthrodesis extending from T3 to L4 with a double pedicle hook/screw and rod construct six months following initial clinical assessment and while the scoliosis had further progressed (Figure 1). An interfacetal and intertransverse arthrodesis was performed bilaterally at every level across the instrumentation using iliac crest graft supplemented by allograft bone. Spinal cord monitoring was performed during the surgery recording somatosensory (SSEP) and motor (MEP) evoked potentials and there were no problems.

panels.rationale: Single chest radiograph in Smith-Magenis Syndrome case report with caption explicitly noting scoliosis of thoracic spine (white arrow), matching vocabulary finding scoliosis with vertebral anomalies. Scoliosis is visible as spinal curvature despite rotation and lung opacities. Lung opacities listed as proposed finding, not vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Alhaj Ali et al. Chronic Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure in a Patient With Smith-Magenis Syndrome: A Case Report.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.72980. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Chest X-ray shows hazy airspace opacities (black arrow) in both lung fields. Scoliosis of the thoracic spine is also noted (white arrow)
in_text_mentions: Chest X-ray revealed bilateral hazy airspace opacities (Figure 1). CT imaging from the previous day showed bilateral ground glass infiltrates and mosaicism (Figure 2). Both imaging studies also revealed scoliosis (Figures 1, 3).
